role: sub-statement: bounded gaps (along consecutive primes ≡ 1 mod 24) for small-C solvability
missing_theorem: ∃ K: among any K consecutive primes p ≡ 1 (24), some p has a (★) word with C ≤ 2. No ES yield (a fixed finite menu with bounded gaps still leaves the other primes). Heuristically FALSE: C ≤ 2 failure needs all prime factors of 4p+1 ≡ 1 (4) and of 8p+1 inside {1,3} or {1,5} (mod 8) (exact for these elementary 2-group levels, Z1561), a set of relative density ≍ (log p)^{−c}; independent-looking runs of K such primes then occur infinitely often for every K. Under Hypothesis H a fixed menu fails i.o., but H does not control consecutiveness, so the run statement is unproved either way.
status_ref: FRONTIER §3 B2 Thm 2.2(iii) (fixed menus fail i.o., CONDITIONAL on H); out_Q11 Z1561 (exact C ≤ 3, 6 failure patterns); Maynard/Shiu-type results on consecutive primes in thin sets (literature lead, not checked)

role: structure lemma: level failure ⟺ prime factors confined to a −1-free subgroup (Galois/Chebotarev-at-a-point shape)
missing_theorem: 'No divisor of 4Cp+1 is ≡ −1 (mod 4C)' ⟺ 'the prime factors generate a subgroup of (ℤ/4C)^× not containing −1'. FALSE in general (⇐ holds, ⇒ fails): multiplicity poverty. EVIDENCE this pass (primes 10³ < p < 2·10⁴, C ≤ 30): among level failures, the share where the factors DO generate −1 is 0 % (ω = 1), 7 % (ω = 2), 39 % (ω = 3), 75 % (ω = 4), 95 % (ω = 5); Pass 1 of Z1443 and Z1512 found 13–21 % over all pairs. The equivalence holds exactly when (ℤ/4C)^× is an elementary 2-group (4C | 24, i.e. C ∈ {1, 2, 3, 6}), where subset products = span.
status_ref: this pass: scripts/z52d_avenue_Q11_g4taxonomy.py (EVIDENCE); out_P01 Z1443 (Pass 1, 13 %); out_Q10 Z0545, Z2935; CLASS_FORCING Thm 2.1 (Galois data see parity, never class)

role: explicit failure taxonomy at the smallest levels (base case of a 'C ≤ K failure ⇒ contradiction' argument)
missing_theorem: Known-true (elementary, this pass): when (ℤ/4C)^× is an elementary abelian 2-group (4C ∈ {4, 8, 12, 24}), subset products of the prime factors equal their span, so level C fails exactly when all prime factors of 4Cp+1 lie in a −1-free subgroup: C = 1: all ≡ 1 (4); C = 2: all in {1, 3} or all in {1, 5} (mod 8); C = 3: all in {1, 5} or {1, 7} (mod 12); C = 6: all in a hyperplane of (ℤ/24)^× ≅ (ℤ/2)³ avoiding 23 (one of the odd real characters trivial on every factor). Each is a Landau-type set of density ≍ (log p)^{−1/2}. The proof architecture 'C ≤ K fails ⇒ contradiction' is a fixed finite menu: false i.o. under H (B2(iii)).

role: group-theoretic precision for the sieve of level failures (maximal −1-free subgroups of (ℤ/4C)^×)
missing_theorem: (Calibration, PROVED here.) Not every −1-free subgroup lies in an index-2 −1-free subgroup: in (ℤ/16)^× = ⟨−1⟩ × ⟨5⟩, H = {1, 7} avoids −1 = 15 but both odd real characters (χ_{−4}, χ_{−8}) equal −1 at 7. So confinement must be stated for −1-free subgroups of any index; since every proper H has |H| ≤ φ/2, the confinement density is (log N)^{|H|/φ − 1} ≤ (log N)^{−1/2}, i.e. index 2 is the worst (half-dimensional) case. Confinement is in any case a minority failure mode for ω ≥ 4 (Z1444).
status_ref: this pass (example verified by hand: 7 ≡ 3 (4) ⇒ χ_{−4}(7) = −1; (−8/7) = (−1/7)(2/7)³ = −1); out_Q11 Z1444

Size bounds restrict the box but give no existence: 'finite check' shapes need a uniform threshold argument, which B1/B2 exclude for fixed menus.

role: sum-product / Bourgain–Glibichuk–Konyagin covering of (ℤ/e)^× by the divisor-ratio set of one N
missing_theorem: For every large p some e-slice has its ratio set {ab⁻¹ mod e : ab | N} large enough (≥ e^δ with multiplicative structure) that sum-product/BGK results force it to contain −1. The ratio set has ≤ 3^{ω(N)} ≈ (log p)^{log 3 + o(1)} elements, so it is ≥ e^δ only for e ≤ polylog; BGK-type covering also needs a subgroup or product set of power size. In the only admissible range (e polylog) the question is the B4 covering problem, where structure-only guarantees are linear in φ(e).
status_ref: LONGSHOT_PIGEONHOLE Prop 1.4 (sharp, PROVED); FRONTIER §3 B4; BRAINSTORM/addcomb_unit_fraction_density.md

role: polynomial method (Dvir, Croot–Lev–Pach) on a finite-field shadow of integral positive certificates
missing_theorem: A statement over F_p (e.g. 'a set S ⊂ F_p² of size ≫ p meets a curve') whose truth implies ES(p). Local (mod p) solvability is free; the ES₅ content is entirely the archimedean size cut — solutions of tuv − u − v ≡ 0 (mod p) with t, u, v ≪ p^{1/3+ε} exist trivially, and ES needs equality, not ≡ 0 (mod p). A finite-field shadow must encode the exact height, which pigeonhole/volume methods cannot (covering needs sub-power windows, (J)85).
status_ref: out_P05 Z2816 (all ES₅ content is the size cut, circular); FRONTIER §3 M1b row ((J)85), §1 (BL: local solvability free); BRAINSTORM/polynomial_method.md

role: Combinatorial Nullstellensatz on a polylog grid of (u, C)
missing_theorem: A polynomial over F_ℓ on the grid {(u, C) : u, C ≤ log p} whose non-vanishing at some grid point implies (4uC − 1) | p + u. FALSE in substance: such a point has witness modulus 4uC − 1 ≤ 4 log²p, but the least Type II witness modulus satisfies W(p) ≥ exp(c(log p)^{1/4}(log log p)^{−1/4}) for infinitely many Mordell-hard primes, so the grid contains no certificate i.o.; two-endpoint polylog windows are false i.o. unconditionally (H4_NOT_POLYLOG).
status_ref: POINTWISE_OMEGA13 Thm 5.1 (PROVED modulo Gallagher, Nair–Tenenbaum, energy bound; FRONTIER §3 B1); FRONTIER §6 'Witness windows bounding both forest endpoints … by (log p)^C → false i.o., unconditionally' (H4_NOT_POLYLOG.md)
note: Any CN grid must be at least exp((log p)^{1/4−ε}) in the witness modulus, where the polynomial's degree makes CN vacuous.

role: percolation/giant-component argument on a divisor graph of {4Cp+1}
missing_theorem: A deterministic graph G_p (vertices: the integers 4Cp+1, C ≤ T, and their divisors; edges: residue relations) in which a certificate is guaranteed once a density exceeds a threshold. Sharp-threshold theorems (Friedgut–Kalai) are statements about random graphs; G_p is deterministic and its edges between different levels exist only through small primes (privacy), so connectivity carries congruence data only; a certificate is one edge of a specific type at one level (B2).
status_ref: FRONTIER §3 'Privacy of large primes' (SS8 Lemma 2.3), B2
barrier: privacy, B2, B6 (threshold theorems are probabilistic averages)
